sentences.text: Shri Rajesh Shukla - Additional Advocate General for re Heard on I.A.No.20169 of 2023, first application under Section 389(1) Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of appellant - Rajeet Kumar Shrivastava.

Present appellant stood convicted under Section 366 A of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for five years' with a fine of Rs.10,000/-, under Section 376(1) of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for ten years' with a fine of Rs.10,000/-, under Section 3(2)5 of SC/ST Act and sentenced to undergo life imprisonment with a fine of Rs.10,000/- and under Section 3(2)(5a) of SC/ST Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for three years' with a fine of Rs.10,000/- with default stipulation, vide judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 14.07.2022 passed by VIth Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act) Bhind District Bhind (M.P.) in SCATR No.14/2020.
The present appellant so far has suffered incarceration of more than four years and three months.
As per prosecution story, on 20.08.2019 parents of the prosecutrix left their house for the work at around 7 am, leaving the prosecutrix at house alone.
When parents of the prosecutrix returned back to their home, at around 5:30 pm, they saw lock on the front door of the house.

Upon asking to their landlord about the lock on their house, the landlord stated that the prosecutrix left the house in the morning at around 9 am by saying that she is going to buy some medicines but she did not return back.
The parents of the prosecutrix searched her at their relatives and nearby places but the prosecutrix could not be traced.
Father of the prosecutrix lodged a complaint at Police Station Malanpur bearing crime No.166/2019 for the offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC.
On the same date, missing report bearing No. 13/2019 was also registered.
During the course of investigation, prosecutrix was recovered on 04.11.2019.
Her statement was recorded and medical examination of the prosecutrix was conducted.
During investigation, it was found that the prosecutrix alongwith her friend had gone to Gole Ka Mandir Gwalior where she met with present appellant.
Friendship was developed between them.
They used to talk with each other on phone.
The appellant wanted to marry with the prosecutrix.

On the pretext of marriage, the appellant took the Rajeet Kumar Shrivastava vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171801480/
1 prosecutrix to Delhi on 20.08.2019 and from Delhi took the prosecutrix to Hisar by train.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellant forced the prosecutrix to marry with him but when the prosecutrix denied, the appellant committed rape upon the prosecutrix and brought her back to Gwalior where the Police recovered the prosecutrix and arrested the appellant and implicated him under Section 363, 366, 376 of IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act and Section 3(2)(5) and 3(2)(5a) of SC/ST Act.
Upon completion of investigation including recording of statements of witnesses, collection of evidence and necessary formalities, challan was filed before the competent Court.
The Special Court, on appreciation of evidence placed on record, convicted and sentenced the present appellant, as referred above.

Learned counsel for the present appellant while taking exception to the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence, submits that learned Special Court has not appreciated the evidence placed on record i n correct perspective.
The judgment suffers from surmises and conjectures.
Present appellant has falsely been implicated in the instant case.
It is further submitted that present appellant has so far undergone incarceration of more than four years and three months.
The appeal being of the year 2022, is not likely to be decided in the near future.

On these grounds,
learned counsel submits that the present appellant may be extended the benefit of suspension of sentence and grant of bail.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor, appearing on behalf of the State, opposed the prayer and prayed for dismissal of suspension application, looking to the nature and gravity of offence.

Upon hearing learned counsel for the parties, though this Court refrains from commenting upon rival contentions touching merits of the case but regard being had to the fact that present appellant so far has already undergone incarceration of more than four years and three months, coupled with the fact that appeal is of the year 2022 and there is no likelihood of early hearing of the appeal in near future, in the obtaining facts and circumstances, we are of the view that present appellant is held entitled to the benefit of suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

Accordingly, I.A.No.20169 of 2023, stands allowed and it is directed that the jail sentence of appellant - Rajeet Kumar Shrivastava shall remain suspended during pendency of the present appeal and he shall be released on bail subject to verification of the factum of depositing the fine amount and on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lac only)
with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court.
Appellant - Rajeet Kumar Shrivastava is directed to appear before the Registry of this Court first on 22/05/2024 and thereafter, on other subsequent dates as may be fixed in this behalf.
Accordingly, the IA stands allowed and disposed of.
Observations on facts, if any, are only for the purpose of deciding the instant I.A. and shall have no bearing on the merits of the appeal.
